# v1.8.0 — scope freeze and legal wording pass

This release narrows STARS Observatory to three analytical layers plus Provenance — per-State supervision burden (attributed State), UN registration lag with its time series, and Article IX incident replays — and revises its legal wording throughout.

- The State dossier and national space legislation layer are withdrawn from the release (preserved on the `dossier` branch).
- "Attributed State (SATCAT owner code, an evidentiary proxy)" replaces "responsible State" wording; a missing UN registration match is described as "no matching UN record", never as a breach.
- The registration panel is reframed as "Registration lag", with the Registration Convention's "as soon as practicable" standard and a caveat on other launching States, intergovernmental organisations, transfers of ownership and GCAT's limits.
- Treaty party status (Outer Space Treaty, Liability Convention, Registration Convention) for each attributed State, sourced solely from UNOOSA, UN Doc A/AC.105/C.2/2026/CRP.9/Rev.1 (as at 1 January 2026).
- Article IX replays describe the fact pattern only and quote the art IX trigger exactly.
- New About tab; footer "© 2026 Hallam Burnapp · Code MIT · Data CC BY 4.0 · About"; citation with URL and accessed date and no institution name.
- Fix: objects with 6-digit catalogue numbers (issued since 11 July 2026) now propagate and appear on the globe.

Full details: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/hallamburnapp-cloud/stars-observatory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Code: MIT. Data and snapshots: CC BY 4.0.
